name: Heel Hook from Carni
summary: The Heel Hook is a rotational leg lock that controls the hip and knee while using an exposed heel as a lever, transmitting rotation through the lower leg.
description: Heel Hook from Carni requires a separate leg entanglement. Carni traps an arm; heel rotation needs controlled hips and knee position before any pressure.
overview:
The attacker has a genuine leg entanglement with the knee line contained and the heel accessible to a controlled upper-body grip. Carni isolates a shoulder with a high leg. A heel-hook attack requires releasing or leaving that configuration and establishing separate hip, knee and heel control.

Confirm that the opponent's leg, rather than an arm or shoulder, is enclosed. Manage distance so the leg cannot move freely through the hold. Keep the knee connected to the entanglement without forcing sideways pressure in a drill. Locate the heel lever without cranking the foot to expose it.

Use only supervised capture-and-release practice with no rotational finish. Check the actual event division; no-gi clothing alone does not make heel hooks legal.

Instructional sources: [Stephan Kesting and Rob Biernacki — three leg-lock control points](https://www.grapplearts.com/three-critical-control-points-leglock/); [Richie Martinez — Carni shoulder lock from Z guard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iClQ2Np-n30).

flashcards.question: Heel hook after Carni: which opposing limb replaces the original arm as the captured target?
flashcards.answer: A single opposing lower limb in leg control. A genuine leg entanglement must be established after leaving Carni's shoulder control. The original wrist-and-triceps clamp does not provide the heel hook.
flashcards.answer_line: A single opposing lower limb in leg control

plausible: The same upper arm without a lower-body capture
Both arms within the high guard triangle
trap: The near shoulder inside the existing overhook

flashcards.question: Heel-hook attack: what is the purpose of controlling the opponent's hip?
flashcards.answer: Limit the leg sliding freely through the entanglement. Hip control manages distance and limits the leg moving freely through the hold. It works with knee-line containment and heel control; it does not replace either of them.
flashcards.answer_line: Limit the leg sliding freely through the entanglement

plausible: Let the knee travel while you hold only the heel
Pull the foot away while leaving their pelvis free
trap: Twist the knee sideways to replace proximal control

flashcards.question: Heel-hook attack: what should happen to the knee line in an unloaded control drill?
flashcards.answer: Stay contained without sideways knee pressure. Keep the knee connected to the entanglement without forcing sideways pressure in a drill.
flashcards.answer_line: Stay contained without sideways knee pressure

plausible: Be pulled sideways while the foot stays fixed
Slide freely beyond the entangling legs
trap: Be ignored once a fingertip touches the heel

plausible: Twist the toes until the heel emerges against resistance

flashcards.answer_line: The heel grip and leg connection

flashcards.question: Heel-hook attack: which joint at the upper end of the leg needs proximal control?
flashcards.answer: The hip above the captured knee. Proximal control manages movement near the pelvis while knee and foot controls act farther along the leg. The three contacts serve different roles.
flashcards.answer_line: The hip above the captured knee

The foot beyond the knee line
trap: The knee alone with the thigh free to travel
